item.title: Lester Trips wants Toronto theatre creators to ‘make it nasty’
item.description: "It doesn’t matter how many reels of a hamster falling out of its cage set to the Requiem I see: The music still hits," says Lauren Gillis. "We joke that the logline for Honey I’m Home is 'normie drone has menty-b from VR Zoom with her own living room.'"

item.title: REVIEW: COC’s elegantly bleak Rigoletto is no laughing matter
item.description: As Rigoletto wept, I became distracted by a lone petal belatedly descending from above. An accident, certainly, but one that offered a reminder of opera’s unpredictable magic: that, even among the grandest of designs, a performance’s final form depends upon these ephemeral moments one calls fate.

item.title: REVIEW: Shakespeare BASH’d brings focus to the mystifying Troilus and Cressida
item.description: This spare, thoughtful staging prioritizes a clarity of text that comes through even when the script’s overall trajectory is less than clear.

item.title: A look inside the flourishing creative life of playwright-actor Pamela Mala Sinha (part one)
item.description: When I learned that the acclaimed artist would be having an action-packed start to 2026, I decided to document this busy period in a trilogy of articles.

item.title: TO Live to present Recirquel’s Paradisum in Toronto
item.description: Next week, a circus-dance hybrid will swing into the Bluma Appel Theatre as part of TO Live’s 2025-26 season.

item.title: REVIEW: In You, Always at Canadian Stage, playfulness meets unabashed emotional vulnerability
item.description: This big-hearted play will steal your favourite going-out shirt, holler your crush’s name at full volume, and then accost you with a bear hug — all the while harboring a deep well of love and resentment.

item.title: REVIEW: Coal Mine’s Eureka Day offers a nuanced portrayal of medical mistrust
item.description: What could possibly urge people to deny experts, doctors, and researchers at the risk of their own life — and the lives of their children? These thoughts swirled through my brain as I entered Coal Mine Theatre to watch the compelling piece of art that is Eureka Day.

item.title: REVIEW: Soulpepper’s Witch is thematically alluring but dramatically thin
item.description: Jen Silverman’s play aspires to communicate something substantive about the human condition — touching on loneliness, ostracization, misogyny, ageism, yearning, and ego — yet it never quite settles on a cohesive or definitive thesis. Lancaster’s production commits to heady visuals and clever idiosyncrasies to fill the gap, with mixed results.

item.title: David Leyshon named interim artistic producer at Lighthouse Festival
item.description: He joins the company as it prepares its 2026 programming, continuing its mandate of producing comedy-driven Canadian theatre in Port Dover and Port Colborne.

item.title: REVIEW: Anusree Roy’s Through the Eyes of God is a fast-paced, one-woman thriller
item.description: This sequel to Pyaasa revisits the themes of motherhood and sacrifice in present-day India through the experience of Chaya, a lower caste Bengali woman.
